info.title: Python TDD workflow with requirement document processing

parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

61: def _ignore_unmatched_kwargs(f: Callable) -> Callable:
62:     """Make function ignore unmatched kwargs.
63: 
64:     If the function already has the catch all **kwargs, do nothing.
65:     """
66:     if _contains_var_kwarg(f):
67:         return f
68: 
69:     @functools.wraps(f)
70:     def inner(**kwargs):
71:         # filter out kwargs that are not part of the function signature
72:         # and transform them to the correct type
73:         filtered_kwargs = {key: _parse(value, key, f) for key, value in kwargs.items() if _is_kwarg_of(key, f)}
74:         return f(**filtered_kwargs)
75: 
76:     return inner
77: 
78: 
79: def _contains_var_kwarg(f: Callable) -> bool:
80:     """Tells whether the given callable contains a keyword argument."""
81:     return any(param.kind == inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD for param in inspect.signature(f).parameters.values())
82: 
83: 
84: def _is_kwarg_of(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
85:     """Tells whether the given `key` identifies a keyword argument of the given callable."""
86:     param = inspect.signature(f).parameters.get(key)
87:     return param is not None and (
88:         param.kind is inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY or param.kind is inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD
89:     )
90: 
91: 
92: def _parse(value: str, key: str, f: Callable) -> Any:
93:     """Parse a value to the correct type.
94: 
95:     Args:
96:         value: The value to parse.
97:         key: The name of the kwarg.
98:         f: The function to parse the value for.
99: 
100:     Returns:
101:         The parsed value.
102: 
103:     """
104:     if _is_str_kwarg_of(key, f) or _is_artifact_loaded(key, f) or _is_output_kwarg(key, f):
105:         return value
106:     try:
107:         type_ = _get_unannotated_type(key, f)
108:         loaded_json_value = json.loads(value)
109: 
110:         if not type_:
111:             return loaded_json_value
112: 
113:         _pydantic_mode = int(os.environ.get("hera__pydantic_mode", _PYDANTIC_VERSION))
114:         if _pydantic_mode == 1:
115:             return parse_obj_as(type_, loaded_json_value)
116:         else:
117:             return TypeAdapter(type_).validate_python(loaded_json_value)
118:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
119:         return value
120: 
121: 
122: def _get_function_param_annotation(key: str, f: Callable) -> Optional[type]:
123:     func_param_annotation = inspect.signature(f).parameters[key].annotation
124:     if func_param_annotation is inspect.Parameter.empty:
125:         return None
126:     return func_param_annotation
127: 
128: 
129: def _get_unannotated_type(key: str, f: Callable) -> Optional[type]:
130:     """Get the type of function param without the 'Annotated' outer type."""
131:     type_ = _get_function_param_annotation(key, f)
132:     if type_ is None:
133:         return None
134:     return unwrap_annotation(type_)

137: def _is_str_kwarg_of(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
138:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` has a type annotation that can be interpreted as a subclass of str."""
139:     if func_param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
140:         return origin_type_issubtype(func_param_annotation, (str, NoneType))
141:     return False
142: 
143: 
144: def _is_artifact_loaded(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
145:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` is actually an Artifact that has already been loaded."""
146:     if param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
147:         if (artifact := get_workflow_annotation(param_annotation)) and isinstance(artifact, Artifact):
148:             return artifact.loader == ArtifactLoader.json.value
149:     return False
150: 
151: 
152: def _is_output_kwarg(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
153:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` is an output Artifact/Parameter."""
154:     if param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
155:         if param_or_artifact := get_workflow_annotation(param_annotation):
156:             return bool(param_or_artifact.output)
157:     return False
158: 
159: 
160: def _sanitize_param_name_for_python(param_name: str) -> str:
161:     """Convert kebab-case parameter names to snake_case for Python compatibility."""
162:     # Convert kebab-case (e.g., "a-but-kebab") to snake_case (e.g., "a_but_kebab")
163:     if param_name is None:
164:         return ""
165:     return re.sub(r'-([a-z])', lambda m: '_' + m.group(1), param_name)

168: def _map_function_annotations(function: Callable, template_inputs: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict:
169:     """Parse annotations to substitute values from Argo for the function parameters.
170: 
171:     For Parameter inputs:
172:     * if the Parameter has a "name", replace it with the function parameter name
173:     * otherwise use the function parameter name as-is
174:     * use the Parameter loader if provided
175:     For Parameter outputs:
176:     * update value to a Path object from the value_from.path value, or the default if not provided
177: 
178:     For Artifact inputs:
179:     * load the Artifact according to the given ArtifactLoader
180:     For Artifact outputs:
181:     * update value to a Path object
182:     """
183:     if _contains_var_kwarg(function):
184:         return template_inputs

186:     function_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {}
187: 
188:     # Iterate over the _function parameters_ and map the template inputs to them
189:     # e.g. for `function=func(param: Annotated[int, Parameter(name="my-param")])`,
190:     # and template_inputs={"my-param": "5"}, the function_kwargs will be {"param": 5}
191:     for func_param_name, func_param in inspect.signature(function).parameters.items():
192:         # Sanitize parameter names from kebab-case to snake_case if needed
193:         sanitized_func_param_name = _sanitize_param_name_for_python(func_param_name)
194:         
195:         if param_or_artifact := get_workflow_annotation(func_param.annotation):
196:             if isinstance(param_or_artifact, Parameter):
197:                 if param_or_artifact.output:
198:                     function_kwargs[func_param_name] = get_annotated_output_param(param_or_artifact)
199:                 else:
200:                     # Look for the parameter in template inputs using multiple approaches:
201:                     # 1. Exact match with parameter name (from annotation)
202:                     # 2. Exact match with function parameter name  
203:                     # 3. Kebab-case to snake_case conversion of annotation name
204:                     # 4. Kebab-case to snake_case conversion of function parameter name
205:                     param_value = None
206:                     param_name_from_annotation = param_or_artifact.name
207:                     
208:                     # Try exact match with annotation name
209:                     if param_name_from_annotation and param_name_from_annotation in template_inputs:
210:                         param_value = template_inputs[param_name_from_annotation]
211:                     # Try exact match with function parameter name
212:                     elif func_param_name in template_inputs:
213:                         param_value = template_inputs[func_param_name]
214:                     # Try kebab-case to snake_case conversion of annotation name
215:                     elif param_name_from_annotation:
216:                         converted_annotation_name = _sanitize_param_name_for_python(param_name_from_annotation)
217:                         if converted_annotation_name in template_inputs:
218:                             param_value = template_inputs[converted_annotation_name]
219:                     # Try kebab-case to snake_case conversion of function parameter name
220:                     elif sanitized_func_param_name in template_inputs:
221:                         param_value = template_inputs[sanitized_func_param_name]
222:                     
223:                     # If we couldn't find the value, check if parameter has a default value
224:                     if param_value is None:
225:                         # Check if parameter has a default value
226:                         if func_param.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty:
227:                             # Use the default value
228:                             function_kwargs[func_param_name] = func_param.default
229:                         else:
230:                             # If we still don't have a value and it's not optional, we should not add it
231:                             # Let the function handle missing parameters naturally
232:                             pass
233:                     else:
234:                         function_kwargs[func_param_name] = load_param_input(param_value, param_or_artifact.loads)
235:             else:
236:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = get_annotated_artifact_value(func_param_name, param_or_artifact)
237:         elif not is_subscripted(func_param.annotation) and issubclass(func_param.annotation, (InputV1, InputV2)):
238:             # We collect all relevant kwargs for the single `Input` function parameter
239:             function_kwargs[func_param_name] = map_runner_input(func_param.annotation, template_inputs)
240:         else:
241:             # Use the kwarg value as-is, with kebab-case to snake_case conversion
242:             if sanitized_func_param_name in template_inputs:
243:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = template_inputs[sanitized_func_param_name]
244:             elif func_param_name in template_inputs:
245:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = template_inputs[func_param_name]
246:             else:
247:                 # If the parameter is not found and has a default value, use it
248:                 if func_param.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty:
249:                     function_kwargs[func_param_name] = func_param.default
250:                 # Otherwise, just leave it out - let the function handle it appropriately
251:                 # But if the function expects this parameter, it will raise a TypeError anyway
252:                 # So we don't need to explicitly handle missing parameters here
253:                 pass
254:     return function_kwargs

257: def _runner(entrypoint: str, template_inputs_list: List) -> Any:
258:     """Run the function defined by the entrypoint with the given list of kwargs.
259: 
260:     Args:
261:         entrypoint: The module path to the script within the container to execute. "package.submodule:function"
262:         template_inputs_list: A list of dicts with "name" and "value" keys, to be mapped to the kwargs of the function.
263: 
264:     Returns:
265:         The result of the function or `None` if the outputs are to be saved.
266:     """
267:     # import the module and get the function
268:     module, function_name = entrypoint.split(":")
269:     function: Callable = getattr(importlib.import_module(module), function_name)
270:     # if the function is wrapped, unwrap it
271:     # this may happen if the function is decorated with @script
272:     if hasattr(function, "wrapped_function"):
273:         function = function.wrapped_function
274: 
275:     # convert the template inputs list to a dict
276:     template_inputs: Dict[str, str] = {}
277:     for kwarg in template_inputs_list:
278:         if "name" not in kwarg or "value" not in kwarg:
279:             continue
280:         # sanitize the key for python
281:         key = cast(str, serialize(kwarg["name"]))
282:         value = kwarg["value"]
283:         template_inputs[key] = value
284: 
285:     function_kwargs = _map_function_annotations(function, template_inputs)
286: 
287:     # The imported validate_arguments uses smart union by default just in case clients do not rely on it. This means that if a function uses a union
288:     # type for any of its inputs, then this will at least try to map those types correctly if the input object is
289:     # not a pydantic model with smart_union enabled
290:     _pydantic_mode = int(os.environ.get("hera__pydantic_mode", _PYDANTIC_VERSION))
291:     if _pydantic_mode == 2:
292:         from pydantic import ConfigDict, validate_call  # type: ignore
293: 
294:         function = validate_call(config=ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True))(function)
295:     else:
296:         if TYPE_CHECKING:
297:             from pydantic.v1 import validate_arguments
298:         else:
299:             if _PYDANTIC_VERSION == 1:
300:                 from pydantic import validate_arguments
301:             else:
302:                 from pydantic.v1 import validate_arguments
303: 
304:         function = validate_arguments(config=dict(smart_union=True, arbitrary_types_allowed=True))(function)
305: 
306:     function = _ignore_unmatched_kwargs(function)

497:     ```
498:     msg="cannot save parameter /tmp/hera-outputs/parameters/my-parameter"
499:     argo=true
500:     error="open /tmp/hera-outputs/parameters/my-parameter: no such file or directory"`
501:     ```

503:     The output annotations are used to write files using the schema:
504:     <parent_directory>/artifacts/<name>
505:     <parent_directory>/parameters/<name>
506:     If the artifact path or parameter value_from.path is specified, that is used instead.
507:     <parent_directory> can be provided by the user or is set to /tmp/hera-outputs by default
508:     """
509:     for dest in output_annotations:
510:         if isinstance(dest, type) and issubclass(dest, (OutputV1, OutputV2)):
511:             if os.environ.get("hera__script_pydantic_io", None) is None:
512:                 raise ValueError("hera__script_pydantic_io environment variable is not set")

514:             for field in get_fields(dest):
515:                 if field in {"exit_code", "result"}:
516:                     continue

526:             path = _get_outputs_path(dest[1])

531:     """Write the output_value as serialized text to the provided path. Create the necessary parent directories."""
532:     # Safeguard against None path
533:     if path is None:

535:         
536:     # Special handling for bytes data

540:         path.write_bytes(output_value)
541:         return
542:     
543:     # Special handling for non-base Pydantic models - use their dumps method if available
544:     from hera.shared._pydantic import BaseModel
